summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted for recurrent epigastric abdominal pain and nausea. She presented with poor oral intake and was initially managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain and nausea medications. Her lipase levels trended downward, indicating improvement in pancreatic inflammation. She was transitioned to oral pain control, advanced to a full diet, and remained stable without further nausea or pain. A brief episode of hypotension resolved with fluid bolus and pain control. Constipation was managed with scheduled stool softeners and laxatives. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her GI specialist and primary care provider, continue her home medications, and monitor for recurrence of symptoms.
